newsitem.title: CANADA: Lufthansa Cargo levies world fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo levies world fuel surcharge.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG (LCA) said on Friday that it will levy a US$0.10 per kilogram surcharge on all freight shipments worldwide, effective November 1, to partly offset rising jet fuel costs.
Lufthansa Cargo spokesman Mel Torre told Reuters from New York that the surcharge on chargeable weight will be levied on all LCA waybills.
"If the cargo requires a Lufthansa cargo waybill, it's going to incur this surcharge," he said.
The charge of 10 cents, or 0.15 marks, per kg will be applied in the equivalent local currency of each origin market, he said.
The flat rate surcharge is the same for a short-haul flight or an intercontinental long-haul, he said.
"Until now, Lufthansa Cargo has been able to avoid passing on the heavier cost burden to customers," he said. "It is no longer able to do that due to the current situation."
Torre said parent Deutsche Lufthansa AG's fuel costs are at a five-year high. World jet fuel prices have risen by almost 50 percent since the beginning of July.
When fuel prices return to where they were in July 1996 before the recent surge, the surcharge will be removed.
The charge will apply to freight moving on Lufthansa Cargo freighters and in the belly of Lufthansa passenger aircraft and applies to all customers, including contract shippers, he said.

The decision to levy a surcharge was taken on Friday by the Lufthansa Cargo executive board in Frankfurt, he said. On Thursday, Torre had said there was no plan "as of this moment" to apply a fuel surcharge.

For transatlantic routes, a 10 cent surcharge would be equivalent to a 7-10 percent rate increase for most major carriers, particularly during the October-December peak shipping season when discounting tend to dry up and full market rates are charged.
